# Discrete-Time Signals {#sec-discrete-time-signals}

A signal is just a list of numbers indexed by an integer. This chapter builds the vocabulary used in the rest of the book.

::: {.callout-note}
## Draft chapter
This chapter is planned but not yet written. The outline below is the
working plan.
:::

## Planned contents

- Sequences and the `x[n]` notation; why the index has no units
- The basic building blocks: impulse, unit step, exponential, sinusoid
- Shifting, scaling, adding and multiplying signals in NumPy
- Energy and power
- Finite-length, periodic and infinite signals, and how code represents each one
- Transforming the time axis: reversal, shifting, compression and expansion of the index
- Even and odd parts of a signal
- A short look at continuous-time signals and how they compare with discrete ones
